links.comparator_used: Institution-built AWS cloud system (remote GPU servers, web app on a laptop secondary monitor) versus the on-site Edge system (local GPU workstation overlaying AI on the main surgical monitor), both running GoNoGoNet in a simulated OR
links.outcome: Usability (task completion, SUS), ergonomics (NASA-TLX, Borg CR-10), cost, and carbon footprint of Edge vs Cloud AI deployment
links.effect: Task completion: Cloud median 100% vs Edge 80% (p = 2.16e-5). SUS: Edge 69.67 vs Cloud 65.33, not significant (p = 0.214). NASA-TLX physical difference 17.33 (p = 0.0004) and frustration difference 14.33 (p = 0.0036), both higher with Cloud. Neck strain higher with Cloud (p = 0.0067); strain in any body part 60% Cloud vs 6.7% Edge. Operational cost about $6.50/h Cloud vs 2.84 cents/h Edge, with equal total cost after ~396 h. Carbon 26.22 g CO2e/h Cloud vs 6.84 g/h Edge when running AI (3.8 g/h idle).
links.tradeoff: Edge needs about $2561 CAD upfront hardware (Cloud $0). Edge had lower deployment task completion and the most interface complaints (mobile app). It also had lower FPS (19.02 vs 28.05), although its latency was lower (52.57 ms vs 101.68 ms end-to-end for Cloud). The Cloud setup used a secondary monitor, which may account for the ergonomic differences. Idle Edge energy use can be avoided by unplugging overnight.
links.quote: Results showed greater deployment task completion with Cloud but increased physical strain, carbon emissions, and operational costs compared to Edge after 396 h of use.
